title: Client credentials grant flow
means: The client credentials grant flow is meant only for server-to-server API requests that use an app access token. If the request succeeds, it returns an access token.

title: Use the authorization code to get a token
means: The second step in this flow is to use the authorization code (see above) to get an access token and refresh token. If the request succeeds, it returns an access token and refresh token.

title: Use the authorization code to get a token: a code the authorize page did not issue
means: code: The code that the /authorize response returned in the code query parameter. Where the page stops (it shows no answer for another code), the twin answers the class's error, as the refresh page's for a refresh token it does not hold.

title: Device code grant flow: the token for an authorized device code
means: This grant_type is the RFC standard urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, which signals our Authorization server that the client is trying to exchange the device code for a refresh_token/access_token pair.

title: How to validate a token
means: To validate a token, send an HTTP GET request to https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/validate. If the token is valid, the request returns HTTP status code 200.

title: Revoking Access Tokens
means: If your app no longer needs an access token, you can revoke it. If the revocation succeeds, the request returns HTTP status code 200 OK (with no body).

title: Revoking Access Tokens: a token the client does not hold
means: 400 Bad Request if the client ID is valid but the access token is not.

title: Revoking Access Tokens: a client ID that is not valid
means: 404 Not Found if the client ID is not valid.
